decisions.reason: As a newly launched core safety-shoe line in the firm’s main business, it is still an attractive option to keep open because uncertainty remains and the firm can support it with existing production and sales capabilities.

The comfort insole is inexpensive to maintain as a complementary accessory, so despite limited evidence and some overlap with other insole products, it is still worth keeping while demand becomes clearer.
The supportive insole faces similar overlap risk and modest visibility, but as a low-cost adjacent product it remains a reasonable option to retain for another period rather than abandon immediately.
Its dedicated page suggests stronger commitment and clearer strategic relevance, so under real options logic the firm would likely continue backing this ergonomic safety-shoe series.

Firefighter and rescue boots are a more specialized and uncertain niche, but they fit the firm’s protective-footwear expertise well enough that a large firm would likely keep the option open a bit longer.

Because it was highlighted on the home page and presented as a flagship direction, management would be very unlikely to withdraw it so soon and would continue investing to learn about its market potential.
